text.p: Malaysian interest rates, which have been on an uptrend this year, may be peaking, Arab-Malaysian Finance Bhd chairman Azman Hashim said on Wednesday.

"The general feeling is that interest rates will be peaking. We think the market situation looks like that for a while now," Azman told reporters after the company's annual and extraordinary meetings. "They probably might stay around these levels for a while."
The benchmark three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate was quoted at 7.35/40 on Wednesday.

Azman said liquidity in the banking system remained flush despite current high rates, which will make the government wary of tightening credit any further. The firm rates attract an inflow of short-term funds seeking high yields that the government deemed inflationary.
But interest rates would not fall too much from current levels as this would spur inflation, he said in response to a question on the trimming of a key interest rate by Public Bank Bhd.
Public Bank on Wednesday trimmed its key base lending rate (BLR) to 9.20 percent from 9.30, saying this was because of lower overall cost of funds.
Azman said Arab-Malaysian Finance's business in financing second hand car sales has not been affected by the higher interest rates, despite slower sales of new cars.
A big chunk of the company's business is from financing the sales of second hand cars, analysts said.
But Azman said there was greater competition from traditional financers of new cars who had also moved into the second car market looking for business.
He expects Arab-Malaysian Finance to be able to sustain its profitability for the half-year to September 30, but he declined to give details.
The finance company plans to open seven more branches by the year's end to add to the existing 85-branch network.
The company reported a 33.8 percent rise in net earnings to 180.7 million ringgit for the year ending March 31, 1996, on turnover of 1.123 billion ringgit.
